content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a comprehensive guideline on the control and elimination of human schistosomiasis, a chronic parasitic disease caused by blood flukes of the genus Schistosoma. This disease remains a significant public health issue in tropical and subtropical regions, including parts of Africa, Asia, the Caribbean, and South America. Approximately 779 million people are at risk of infection, with millions requiring preventive chemotherapy annually. The guideline provides evidence-based recommendations to assist countries in achieving morbidity control and elimination of schistosomiasis as a public health problem, with the ultimate goal of interrupting transmission. It emphasizes the importance of preventive chemotherapy, improved access to clean water, sanitation, hygiene education, environmental management, and snail control. The guideline also addresses the use of diagnostic tools in low-transmission areas and strategies for evaluating progress toward elimination. The WHO strategy aligns with the organization's 13th General Programme of Work (2019–2023) and the 2020 roadmap for neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), which targets the elimination of schistosomiasis as a public health problem by 2030. The guideline was developed following the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2014) and involved a multidisciplinary group of experts. Key questions were formulated using the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome) framework, and evidence was systematically reviewed to inform the recommendations. The guideline also updates and supersedes previous WHO publications on schistosomiasis control and elimination. The recommendations are intended for policymakers, national NTD control programs, and task forces within health ministries, as well as regional program review groups and implementation partners. The guideline serves as a reference for stakeholders, including WHO, pharmaceutical manufacturers, donor organizations, and non-governmental organizations, to support efforts in controlling and eliminating schistosomiasis globally.
